chapter.title: Food Industry Residues and Prepared Animal Feed

page.h1: HTS Chapter 23: Food Industry Residues and Prepared Animal Feed — U.S. Exports & Foreign Tariffs

seo.title: Chapter 23 Exports: U.S. Soybean Meal, DDGS & Pet Food Trade | Foreign Tariffs
seo.shortDescription: How much the U.S. exports of Chapter 23 feed products (soybean meal, DDGS, pet food and prepared animal feed), who buys them, and what Canada, Mexico, China and other buyers charge.

intro:
The U.S. exported **$13.65 billion** of Chapter 23 goods in 2025, down **5.4%** from 2024 and 14% below the 2023 peak. Three products make up almost all of it: **soybean meal (36%)**, **pet food and prepared animal feed (31%)** and **distillers’ dried grains (DDGS) and other starch and brewing residues (25%)**. Canada and Mexico take 30%, mostly pet food and soybean meal, while Colombia (+20%) and the Philippines (+49%) were the growth markets.

Tariffs matter little for most of this trade. Canada, Mexico, Colombia and Korea buy duty-free under U.S. trade agreements, and Viet Nam, the Philippines and Japan charge 0–2% on meal and DDGS even without one. **China is the exception**: an extra 10% on every U.S. good on top of its normal rate, plus anti-dumping and countervailing duties that have shut out U.S. DDGS, and U.S. sales there fell 24% in 2025. What usually decides access instead is the buyer’s veterinary and feed approval, especially for pet food.

keyTakeaways: Three products are almost the whole chapter: soybean meal ($4.86B in 2025), pet food and prepared feed ($4.24B) and DDGS ($2.77B).
Canada and Mexico, the two largest buyers, pay nothing on qualifying goods under USMCA, so the certificate of origin is what protects the sale; without it Mexico charges 10–15% on most feed lines.

China is the only top buyer charging more than in January 2025: an extra 10% on all U.S. goods, with its 24-point suspension now running to January 10, 2027 and its exclusions from older counter-tariffs ending December 31, 2026.
The one tariff cut abroad is the EU’s new 40,000-tonne duty-free quota for several U.S. pet food and feed lines, open since July 1, 2026.
